questions.question_text: The point $P\left(\dfrac{8}{17},\dfrac{15}{17}\right)$ lies on the unit circle, and $O$ is the origin. Find the gradient of $OP$ and hence $\tan\theta$, where $\theta$ is the angle of inclination of $OP$.

options.why: Computed run over rise instead of rise over run.
Multiplied the coordinates instead of dividing $y$ by $x$.
Gave the rise alone instead of dividing it by the run.
Ignored the negative run; $P$ is left of the $y$-axis, so the run is negative.
Computed run over rise instead of rise over run.
Added the signed coordinates, $0.6+(-0.8)=-0.2$, instead of dividing rise by run.

questions.question_text: For which of these angles is $\tan\theta$ undefined?

options.why: $\cos180^{\circ}=-1\ne0$, so $\tan180^{\circ}=0$, not undefined.
$\cos360^{\circ}=1\ne0$, so $\tan360^{\circ}=0$, not undefined.
$\cos45^{\circ}\ne0$, so $\tan45^{\circ}$ is defined.

questions.solution_text:
$\tan\theta$ is undefined when $\cos\theta=0$.
At $270^{\circ}$, $P=(0,-1)$, so $\cos270^{\circ}=0$ and $\tan270^{\circ}$ is undefined.

questions.question_text: On the unit circle, $\tan\theta$ equals which of the following?

options.why: Inverted the quotient; $\tan\theta$ is the $y$-over-$x$ gradient, $\dfrac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}$.
Multiplied the coordinates; the gradient is $y$ divided by $x$.
Subtracted the coordinates; the gradient is $y$ divided by $x$.

questions.solution_text:
$\tan\theta$ is the gradient of $OP=\dfrac{y}{x}$, and since $y=\sin\theta$, $x=\cos\theta$:
$\tan\theta=\dfrac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}$

questions.question_text: The point $P\left(-\dfrac{15}{17},\dfrac{8}{17}\right)$ lies on the unit circle, and $O$ is the origin. Find the gradient of $OP$ and hence $\tan\theta$, where $\theta$ is the angle of inclination of $OP$.

options.why: Ignored the negative run; a positive rise divided by a negative run is negative.
Computed run over rise instead of rise over run.
Multiplied the coordinates instead of dividing $y$ by $x$.

options.text: Because $\cos90^{\circ}=0$ and dividing by $0$ is undefined.

options.why: $\sin90^{\circ}=1$, not $0$; it is $\cos90^{\circ}$ that equals $0$.

options.text: Because $90^{\circ}$ lies outside the unit circle.
options.why: $90^{\circ}$ is a valid angle at $(0,1)$; the issue is that $\cos90^{\circ}=0$.
At $90^{\circ}$ the radius is vertical, whose gradient is undefined, not $0$.

questions.solution_text:
$\tan\theta=\dfrac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}$.
At $90^{\circ}$, $P=(0,1)$, so $\cos90^{\circ}=0$ and $\tan90^{\circ}=\dfrac{1}{0}$, which is undefined.

questions.question_text: The point $P\left(\dfrac{12}{37},-\dfrac{35}{37}\right)$ lies on the unit circle, and $O$ is the origin. Find the gradient of $OP$ and hence $\tan\theta$, where $\theta$ is the angle of inclination of $OP$.

options.why: Ignored the negative rise; the point is below the $x$-axis.
Computed run over rise instead of rise over run.
Multiplied the coordinates instead of dividing $y$ by $x$.
